8-month history of 'spasms' in his throat
difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Hypometric saccades
Truncal and limb ataxia
Decreased vibratory sense with inability to ambulate
Bradykinesia and mild rigidity
Palatal myoclonus at a frequency of 1-2 Hz
Patient was unable to stop myoclonus of the palate with voluntary use of the palatal musculature
No clicking was noted by patient or examiners

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of palatal myoclonus and inability to voluntarily suppress it are characteristic of this condition.
The combination of ataxia, parkinsonism, and autonomic dysfunction, along with severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, supports this diagnosis.
The patient's progressive ataxia and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy are consistent with this diagnosis, which is a subtype of multiple system atrophy.

support_spans: Palatal myoclonus at a frequency of 1-2 Hz

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of palatal myoclonus and inability to voluntarily suppress it, without any other identifiable cause, support this diagnosis.
It explains the decreased vibratory sense with inability to ambulate due to potential damage to the cerebellum or its connections.
It explains the normal results of testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12, as this condition is a distinct form of ataxia with myoclonus.
